title: Polynomial base changes test universal openness of an affine morphism
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and put $f=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}(C)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For $n\geq0$, let $\varphi_n:A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to C[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ be the coefficientwise extension of $\varphi$, sending every variable to the corresponding variable [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; the case $n=0$ means $\varphi$ itself. If every $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)$ is an open map, then $f$ is universally open: for every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and every morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, the projection $\operatorname{Spec}(C)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}T\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product] sends open subsets to open subsets. No finiteness, reducedness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A,C$, or $T$.

source.place: Tag 0F31, lemma-test-universally-open, implication (3) => (1), specialized to an affine morphism; the proof explicitly identifies polynomial extensions and arbitrary affine tensor base changes

proof.text: Fix any commutative $A$-algebra $B$. Set $D=B\otimes_A C$, $j:B\to D$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, and $q_B=\operatorname{Spec}(j)$; for $g\in D$ write $D_D(g)=\{\mathfrak p:g\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Apply [lem-sfb-tensor-principal-polynomial-model] to $g$ to obtain finite $n$, $h\in S=C[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, and $e:A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B$ with $q_B(D_D(g))=\operatorname{Spec}(e)^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)(D_S(h)))$. The set $D_S(h)$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. Its image is open by the assumed openness of every $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}(e)$ is continuous, $q_B(D_D(g))$ is open. This holds for every $B,g$, without finiteness assumptions.

source.place: Tag 0F31, lemma-test-universally-open, proof of (3) implies (1), affine algebra paragraph, lines 21755--21784

proof.text: For every commutative $A$-algebra $B$ and every $g\in D_B=B\otimes_A C$, step 1 proves that $q_B(D_{D_B}(g))$ is open. These are exactly the quantified hypotheses of [lem-sfb-principal-affine-test-universally-open] for the given $A\to C$, with the same tensor multiplication and map $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Its conclusion therefore makes $\operatorname{Spec}(C)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}T\to T$ open for every scheme $T$ and every morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. This is the required universal openness.
